Parusahan Saya (R54)

Checked 2026-10-13 · Local mod v1.37.5.0 · Survey-table region: Rahen.

Story quality: High, primarily based on local narrative; mission tree: 44 directly defined missions; current installation supports v1.37.5.0, exact author update date unverified; distinctiveness: High, with overlord relations, favours, and borrowed troops forming a clear diplomatic-development loop; tedium (lower is smoother): Medium, with diplomatic, research, or event-state gates; opening pressure: 69/100, not an in-game difficulty test; expansion demand: 71/100, combining war and management.

v2.1: E68 · A84 · M/T87 · I72 · P32; values: Neutral (51), stable. These five axes are not a four-letter type. See the separate conditional v2.2 route profiles.

Player overview

Parusahan Saya is a Rahen campaign centred on court politics and diplomatic resources. You begin within the Harimraj monarchy and its overlord system, managing favours, borrowed troops, and construction before mages, dynastic politics, and an oracle shape the country's future. It is neither a merchant republic nor simply a conquest tree for a large cat: its distinctive feature is turning diplomatic relations into project financing and political development. The current version also has clearly incomplete nodes; this is not a campaign in which every ending can be completed.

Historical background and the 1444 position

Starting identity in the local history files: R54 begins as a monarchy with the Prabhi reform, Royal Harimari primary culture, accepted Rabhidarubsad culture, the High Philosophy faith, and the Golden Palace school. Its capital is province 4415. Hemantsenar I of the Iron Stripe dynasty rules, and heir Vijaysen has a claim of 100. The country history also initializes the caste estate and national mage privileges.

Diplomatic history explicitly records R51 as its overlord in 1444, with the relationship type daimyo_vassal. This is more direct evidence than the appearance of the word “overlord” in a mission: the player is a monarch operating inside an existing hierarchy, not an independent free city. The 1500 end date in the static diplomatic-history record is not a promise that an event automatically grants independence in 1500.

No dedicated Parusahan Saya history page was retrieved. I read a related section of the offline Wiki's Wars of the Vizierate, which provides regional context but not a full account of this country's origins. Its founding date and early dynastic genealogy are therefore not guessed. The opening configuration above also does not establish the actual rights held by every caste member.

Distinctive mechanics and pace

The “Beneficial Benefactors” mission connects diplomatic favours with construction of a Ruby Garden. Under the relevant conditions, reaching 50 favours has both parties contribute 500 ducats; other favour thresholds use different tiers. If the target already has a level-one garden, the province effect follows a different branch. Diplomacy is therefore not merely support for a future war: it can fund domestic construction directly.

You also manage the overlord relationship and borrowed troops, while bringing mages into government and tying court factions and legitimacy to mission progress. Iron, military development, and dynastic ambitions add another layer: the country pursues material strength as well as the legitimacy to shape Rahen politics. Its identity comes from these interacting loops, not merely from the words “Golden Palace.”

The country's own mission file has 44 exclusive missions. The structured country package reports 50 because it includes six shared Raheni missions. This article does not count shared content as original country-tree length, nor does it audit every individual reward. Diplomacy, construction, and event progression overlap, so mission count alone does not translate directly into campaign duration.

Mission-tree future and incomplete content

The future tree brings a mage court, Iron Stripe military politics, an oracle, and conflict over the throne into the campaign. The oracle event flavor_parusahan_saya.103 has only one option: it sets oraclemission_flag and swaps the mission tree. Although the Iron King and oracle mission groups have different potential conditions, that alone does not prove the player can choose freely between two permanently exclusive endings.

In particular, “Rise of the Iron King” has always=no in its trigger. Its effects do include a later event, but the trigger cannot be satisfied through ordinary mission progression in the checked script. The encyclopedia can describe the intended direction, but cannot present it as a fully playable ending or construct a complete Iron King personality branch from this incomplete node.

This does not mean the whole country is unplayable: the verified diplomacy, favours, construction, and court missions remain real. But players who expect an uninterrupted campaign in which every final mission can be completed should treat this source-level limitation as a material caveat. No modified save was used to bypass the condition, and no later developer plans are inferred from it.

National personality and values

The baseline is centralised royal power, a regional political ambition, and a strong magical-court theme; construction is not the sole goal. The pluralism score is limited because of the caste and dynastic structures, not because a tiger-people state is assumed to reject every outsider. Compared with Kheionai, the evidence here emphasises existing court resources and mage politics rather than clearly enacted broad social reform.

Values are provisionally Neutral. Public works, cooperative exchange, and competition for power coexist, while direct country-specific evidence for comprehensive enslavement or deliberate destruction has not been established. Caste labels, monarchy, and military ambitions do not by themselves imply evil. The incomplete ending is not an action that has already occurred, and the oracle phase does not automatically add a new good or evil score.

Development context, player feedback, and caveats

Official Dev Diary 105 discusses the country in substance and can inform its design intent and the context of Raheni reform; the 2026 release introduction cannot override the current local script's permanently false trigger. This review found one directly relevant 2026 player discussion, concerning a point where early missions stalled after the overlord order collapsed. The number of relevant discussions is one; unrelated material is not added merely to make a pair.【Development context】【Community view】

Recommended for players who enjoy court events, diplomatic financing, and Raheni hierarchical politics. The caveats are progression tied to events and overlord status, plus the verified incomplete ending. Not every state combination was tested in-game; one player's stalled campaign does not prove that every save will stall.

Sources, search scope, and open questions are documented in the evidence record.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces current national traditions, seven national ideas and ambition. Traditions apply on adoption, ideas unlock through investment, and ambition follows completion of all seven. Only national ideas are listed, not racial, governmental or mission bonuses; predecessor and successor sets do not stack. Idea descriptions can recall history or describe future ideals and do not automatically establish events before 1444.

Effect displays and units are inherited for source parity, not independently certified; uncertain percentages remain accompanied by script keys and raw values.

Parusahan Sayai Traditions

  • global_manpower_modifier：+15% (global_manpower_modifier; raw value 0.15).

  • Army maintenance modifier: -10% (land_maintenance_modifier; raw value -0.1).

1. The Great Grain Palace

Unlike most of the palace names of Inner Rahen, our home has a justly pragmatic title. The lands of Parusahan Saya are part of the great Raheni bread basket, the food grown here just as vital to civilization along the Dhenbasana as the better known cotton crop.

In addition to ensuring that our people are well fed, the constant industry of trading and shipping wheat up and down the Dhenbasana has made the folk here adepts at moving large quantities of victuals and other goods quickly and efficiently.

  • Land force limit modifier: +5% (land_forcelimit_modifier; raw value 0.05).

  • National Supply Limit Modifier: +20% (global_supply_limit_modifier; raw value 0.2).

2. The Iron Stripe

Born in 1370, Vasudevar of the Imperious Stripe was the seventh son of the of then-Prabhi of Ghundagar. Small as a child, he was seen as a disappointment to his tutors – he had no skill in writing, no patience for books, no interest in learning the finer points of administration. But when he first took the field of battle to lead his father’s men during the Moderationist Revolt, his destiny became apparent.

A natural born leader, a brilliant tactical mind, and a skilled and utterly unflinching warrior despite his diminutive size, Vasuvedar led his soldiers to victory time and time again, rapidly rising the ranks. Noticed by Amanapurna the Bloody himself for his successes, particularly on the field at the decisive battle of Satarsaya, he was elevated to his own Prabhia position on land once held by the Setarbul and bestowed with the clan name Iron Stripe for his noted willpower and resolve.

  • morale_damage_received：-10% (morale_damage_received; raw value -0.1).

3. The Battle of Satarsaya

In the year 1401, the combined moderationist armies assembled upon the Plains of Satarsaya, some thirty-thousand men strong, opposed only by the twelve-thousand Iron Tigers of Vasuvedar. Their elephants and horses charged us, but they fell and broke their legs in the concealed ditches we had prepared, and we waited. The enemy pelted us with arrows and sling bullets, but they pinged harmlessly off our unusually large shields, and still we waited.

When this bombardment failed, our foes charged us, but their charge was slowed, broken by the ditches; only then did we finally pounce. Nearly half of the rebel host fell to the army of the Iron Stripe, and the backbone of Dalapalar’s rebellion was broken. It was this battle that built the Iron Stripe’s legacy, and this commitment to discipline that remains at the core of its military tactics to this day.

  • Discipline: +5% (discipline; raw value 0.05).

4. The Compact of Sephahan

Though their land was won by Vasuvedar at Setarsaya, it was kept by the diplomatic prowess of his son Hemantsenar. Recognizing the vulnerable location of his holdings, Hemantsenar spent the four decades of his reign building a network of friendships, alliances, and spy networks across Rahen. These alliances built Parusahan Saya’s power and influence far beyond what could be expected of the small state, and Hemantsenar and his heirs were regular guests of Senaptia, great Ministers, and even the Raja himself.

The alliance network formed the backbone of the resistance to the ascension of Ramapalar III in 1481, and was formalized into the Compact of Sephahan, by Amtujsaat when they declared Indira of the Bloody Claw unfit to serve as first minister and started the Wars of the Vizierate.

  • Diplomatic relations: +1 (diplomatic_upkeep; raw value 1).

5. The Secret Heirs of Acay the Younger

In 1487, the first War of the Vizierate ended at the Battle of Nabukh. Acay the Younger, Raja of the Gold Banner, was slain on the field by the Greens, and his young son trampled in the rout that followed. Despite their many early successes, the fortunes of the Golds were utterly reversed by Nabukh, and the months that followed would see the grudging re-establishment of peace under Ramapalar III.

Unknown to the courts of Rahen, however, Acay’s line was not extinguished at Nabukh. His daughter Aysha, believed lost in the same chaos that claimed her brother, had managed to escape the battlefield and fled to the court of Parusahan Saya. There she would live in hiding, wedding the young lord Kitir of the Iron Stripe, and birthing two sons by him – Golpalar and Hemantsen. The princess would tragically die at only 23 following the birth of her younger child, and missed seeing both boys return the line of Acay the Younger to the Lotus Throne in the coming decades.

  • Diplomatic reputation: +100% (diplomatic_reputation; raw value 1).

  • Improve relations: +10% (improve_relation_modifier; raw value 0.1).

6. The Storming of Dhenijansar

When Ramparlar III was assassinated in 1495, his ineffectual and foppish son Vijayswanath II took the throne. As his rule progressed and saw the young man dominated by his vizier and ministers, Kitir of the Iron Stripe saw an opportunity to press his son Golpalar’s claim to the throne. Calling together the old gold banner faction, Kitir revealed the true parentage of his children, rallied his banners, and secured alliances with the Golden Paw and Starry Eye clans with betrothals between their daughters and his sons.

In the spring of 1498, the Iron Tiger pounced and infiltrated the fortress of Dhurajilala in a swift and brutal campaign. Making extensive use of sappers, the city of Dhenijansar fell before him in just 6 weeks, and Vijayswanath II was forced to flee. The Iron Stripes and Golden Paw led a great triumph through the streets of the capital that culminated with the 6-year Goparlar III sitting the Lotus Throne as the first Iron Raja.

  • Leader siege: +1 (leader_siege; raw value 1).

  • Siege ability: +5% (siege_ability; raw value 0.05).

7. Reforms of the Iron Raja

Hemantsen of the Iron Stripe ascended the Lotus Throne at the age of 19. Unexpectedly inheriting the throne from his brother Gopalar III, his energy and optimism were a galvanizing force that powered the recovery that the Raj would experience in the first half of the 16th century. With the aid of his wife, Rani Jira of the Starry Eye, sweeping changes to the Raj's structure were enacted - the vizier was disempowered, the ministries reformed, and the armies of the realm modernized and centralized. These military reforms, incorporating lessons of the Wars of Vizierate and the elevations of the new senapti of Tujgal, Amtujsaat, and Banjisbid, allowed the Raj to repel the Jaddari at the Shenral pass in 1522 and push The Command back from Eastern Dhujat in a pair of wars waged during the 1530s.

After the death of Rani Jira in 1556, however, Hemantsen's mind would begin to slow and much of the Raja's power would again fall to the Vizier, the Senapti of Amtujsaat. Ambitious lords restarted the short-sighted intrigues of the 1400s, culminating when the Imperious Stripes of Ghundagar triggered the 1561 Dhenbasana Uprising that marked the beginning of the end for the second Harimraj.

  • Reform progress growth: +20% (reform_progress_growth; raw value 0.2).
